payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: If the source paper is not visibly stuffed inside the source cup, is there visible progress toward stuffing that paper into that cup?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image shows the matched source paper being moved toward or into the matched source cup, but not yet visibly stuffed inside it. Fail if the matched objects are assessable and there is no visible progress toward placing the paper into the cup, or the paper is already visibly stuffed inside it. Unknown if the source objects cannot be reliably matched in the edited image, or their placement or movement cannot be assessed.
node.binding: Identify the requested paper and cup by their visual and contextual roles in the source image, allowing their appearance to change in the edited image. Count only visible progress toward stuffing that paper into that cup; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows a white paper and a blue cup. In the edited image, the paper has been moved over and partly into the matched cup, showing progress toward stuffing it, but it is not visibly stuffed inside.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague to preserve object identity across the source and edited images. The trace says the source white paper and blue cup cannot be reliably matched to the edited blue printed item and round object, yet support 2 treats them as matched and credits partial progress. Tighten the binding/criteria to require evidence that the edited objects are the same paper and cup, and that the paper has actually moved toward or into that cup; do not infer progress from merely nearby objects. Keep completion distinct from partial progress: paper on or near the rim is not proof it is stuffed inside. When identity or placement is genuinely unresolved, retain unknown rather than forcing a label. The reference ‘no’ constrains the aggregate but is not atomic evidence; investigate the conflicting support judgments rather than encoding ‘no’ as the answer. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported, so focus the repair on binding and evidence consistency.

response.content: {"text":"Repair the binding so it identifies the source paper and cup by their visible attributes and requires reliable cross-image identity, not merely objects with similar roles. Here the source has a white sheet and a blue cup; the edited image shows a blue printed item and a round reddish object. The trace’s claim that these are matched—and that the paper is partly in the cup—is not supported by the images. Do not count proximity or an apparent paper-like shape as progress without evidence that it is the same paper being placed toward the same cup. Keep the node’s partial-progress criterion distinct from completion, and return unknown when identity or placement cannot be assessed. Treat the aggregate “no” as a constraint to investigate, not as atomic ground truth or a reason to force a negative. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; focus the structural edit on binding and evidence thresholds."}
